text:
maya: Quick sync — ran a focused bakeoff across AWQ-int8 / GPTQ-int8 / FP8 targeting short-prompt SQL->text and CSV-serialize workloads. Seeing a repeatable "token splintering"/duplication issue in AWQ-int8 on prompts <= 30 tokens.

maya: Repro example (short):
```
input: Convert: SELECT id,name FROM users WHERE id=5
AWQ-int8: Convert : SELECT id , name FROM users WHERE id = 5
GPTQ-int8: Convert: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id=5
FP8: Convert: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id=5
```

maya: Note the extra spaces and comma split into separate tokens and occasional duplicate columns. Not typical for longer prompts. Hits our formatting-sensitive evals (sql2text, csv-export).

maya: Eval summary (subset, prompt_len <=30, 6k examples in quick run):
```
AWQ-int8    exact_match: 82.1%   formatting_fidelity: 68.3%   halluc_rate: 3.2%
GPTQ-int8   exact_match: 84.9%   formatting_fidelity: 88.0%   halluc_rate: 1.9%
FP8         exact_match: 85.3%   formatting_fidelity: 89.1%   halluc_rate: 1.7%
```

maya: Config: runtime=serve-1.6, batch_size=1, kv_cache=warmstart=off, quant_profile=awq-smallprompt-v2, model=redwood/open-7b-v2

owen: Oof. Did you try toggling prefix_cache or increasing batch to encourage different tokenization alignment? :thinking:
own: Also what hardware and kernel?

maya: HW: p4d-dedicated pool (dedicated-redispatch), kernel set from runtime auto. I tried batch=4 quickly — metric drops slightly on latency but formatting_fidelity improves ~+3pt, still worse than GPTQ. prefix_cache toggling helped marginally.

liam: Could this be an artifact of AWQ's quant mapping for comma/whitespace tokens? Short prompts have tight alignment; quant noise may push softmax mass to adjacent tokens. Any logits dumps?

maya: Grabbed a couple. Example logits slice around comma token (token ids anonymized):
```
step=12 tokens=[..., 44(comma), 12(space), 98(name), ...]
AWQ logits: [..., -1.9, -2.1, -0.4]  -> picks space then comma as separate tokens
GPTQ logits: [..., -0.3, -0.2, 2.1]   -> picks comma then name
```

maya: Looks like AWQ makes comma and surrounding whitespace less confident for this prefix.

tara: Are customer-facing routes affected? Which deployment profiles?

maya: Mostly affects short-format routes: csv-export, table-serialize, and some legalqa short answers. Hosted API users with default `compact` profile may see it in edge cases. Dedicated reserved pools with larger batch warmstart less impacted.

owen: Can you drop a minimal reproducer (curl/python) + seed so infra can run across kernels? I'll spin a matrix across kernels (cuBLAS/auto), rounding modes.

maya: putting snippet below — reproducible with the public sample prompt + seed=42: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"open-7b-v2-awq","prompt":"Convert: SELECT id,name FROM users WHERE id=5","max_tokens":40,"seed":42,"batch_size":1}'
```

liam: If it's token-mass shift, we could try local per-token rescaling (temperature per token) as a mitigation in the runtime; also test AWQ quant params (num-buckets, group-size). Worth a quick ablation: AWQ num-buckets 256 -> 512, group 128 -> 64.

maya: On it. I'll run ablations overnight and push results here. If anyone wants the full logits + example set (6k), say so and I'll drop a bucket in S3.

eval-bot: New issue created: INF-4392 "AWQ-int8 token-splintering on short prompts (sql/csv)". Assigned to maya, triage to eng-ml + eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4392

tara: Thanks — please add clear repro + the minimal curl so support can triage customer reports.

owen: I'll add an infra job to sweep kernels + quant variants, will tag results in the ticket.

maya: Thanks — prioritizing this as medium. Will post ablation summary first thing. :white_check_mark:
